title: Forces - 123 school
heading: Forces
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: What is the unit of force?
questions.a: Newton (N)

questions.q: What do you use to measure a force?
questions.a: A newton meter (force meter)

questions.q: Name three types of force
questions.a: Gravity, friction, spring force, muscle force, magnetic force

questions.q: What can a force do to an object?
questions.a: Change its speed, its direction or its shape

questions.q: What is the force called with which the Earth pulls on an object?
questions.a: Gravity (force of gravity)

questions.q: Give the formula for the force of gravity
questions.a: Fz = m × g

questions.q: What is the value of g on Earth?
questions.a: 9.8 N/kg

questions.q: An object has a mass of 10 kg. What is the force of gravity on Earth?
Which unit goes with mass?
questions.a: Kilogram (kg)

questions.q: You go to the Moon. Does your mass change?
questions.a: No. The force of gravity on you does become smaller.

questions.q: What is friction force?
questions.a: A force that opposes a motion

questions.q: What is spring force?
questions.a: The force with which a stretched or compressed spring pushes or pulls back

questions.q: What does the spring constant tell you?
questions.a: How stiff a spring is (how much force you need for a certain extension)

questions.q: A spring stretches 2 cm under 4 N. How many cm does it stretch under 8 N?
questions.a: 4 cm

questions.q: What is the resultant force?
questions.a: The single force that has the same effect as all the forces together

questions.q: A force of 30 N acts to the right and 20 N to the left. What is the resultant force?
questions.a: 10 N to the right

questions.q: How large is the resultant force when the forces are balanced?
questions.a: 0 N

questions.q: How do you draw a force?
questions.a: As an arrow: the length shows the size, the arrow points in the direction and starts at the point of application

questions.q: What is a lever?
questions.a: A bar that can turn about a pivot

questions.q: What is the pivot?
questions.a: The point about which a lever turns

questions.q: What is the lever arm of a force?
questions.a: The distance from the pivot to the force

questions.q: Which formula applies when a lever is balanced?
questions.a: Force × arm on the left = force × arm on the right

questions.q: A lever is balanced. On the left, 200 N acts at 1.0 m from the pivot. On the right, 100 N acts. At what distance?
Why do you need less force to loosen a nut with a long spanner?
questions.a: A long spanner has a long arm

questions.q: Name two objects that are levers
questions.a: Crowbar, scissors, pliers, seesaw, wheelbarrow

questions.q: What is the counterweight of a tower crane for?
questions.a: To keep the crane balanced

questions.q: Calculate the force of gravity on a child of 40 kg. Use g = 9.8 N/kg.
A force of gravity of 29.4 N acts on an object. Use g = 9.8 N/kg. What is the mass?
On the Moon g = 1.6 N/kg. What is the force of gravity on an object of 10 kg?
A spring becomes 3.0 cm longer under a force of 6.0 N. How much longer does the spring become under 10 N? (the spring stays within its elastic range)
questions.a: Extension is proportional to force: 3.0 × 10 / 6.0 = 5.0 cm

questions.q: A lever is balanced. On the left, 50 N acts at 0.40 m from the pivot. On the right the arm is 0.25 m. What is the force on the right?
questions.a: F<sub>1</sub> × r<sub>1</sub> = F<sub>2</sub> × r<sub>2</sub>; 50 × 0.40 = F × 0.25; F = 80 N

questions.q: What is the moment of a force of 20 N on an arm of 0.30 m?
What does a fixed pulley do?
questions.a: It changes the direction of the force; the force stays the same size

questions.q: You lift a load of 200 N with a movable pulley (no friction, ropes vertical). How large a force must you exert?
questions.a: A movable pulley halves the force: 100 N (but you pull twice as much rope)

questions.q: A crate of 20 kg is at rest on the ground. Use g = 9.8 N/kg. How large is the force of the ground on the crate?
questions.a: The crate is at rest: the force of the ground is equal to the force of gravity: 20 × 9.8 = 196 N
